nodes.label: Webview Wrapper Architecture
nodes.rationale: Embed each service's official web app in a WebContentsView. Chosen over native protocol clients (only Telegram has an official personal API; reverse-engineered WhatsApp/Messenger/Discord libs violate ToS and risk account bans; Zalo has nothing) and hybrid TDLib+webviews (complexity for marginal gain).

nodes.label: Electron Desktop Shell Decision
nodes.rationale: Electron (latest stable) chosen over Tauri v2 (two webview engines to test, weaker multi-webview session isolation, some chat web apps degrade on non-Chrome engines) and CEF (too much plumbing); bundled Chromium gives identical rendering on macOS and Windows.

nodes.label: Per-Service Session Isolation
nodes.rationale: Each service gets a persistent partition (persist:<id>) so cookies, logins, and storage never bleed across services; login sessions survive restarts.

nodes.label: Chrome User-Agent Override
nodes.rationale: Strip the Electron/app tokens and present a current plain Chrome UA — required because WhatsApp Web and Google-family login flows block unknown user agents.

nodes.label: Service Hibernation
nodes.rationale: Destroys webContents of background services idle > N minutes (default 30) to mitigate RAM growth with five web apps; WhatsApp/Zalo default to never-hibernate because hibernated services cannot count unread or notify.

nodes.label: Unread Count Recipes
nodes.rationale: Small per-service DOM scripts adapted from ferdium-recipes (Apache-2.0) that extract {direct, indirect} unread counts on an interval; fixture-backed tests so a service redesign shows up as a red test, not a silently wrong badge.

nodes.label: Title-Parse Fallback / Stale Dot
nodes.rationale: If DOM badge selectors break, fall back to parsing '(N)' from the document title; if that also fails, show a neutral 'count may be stale' dot instead of a wrong number.

nodes.label: Unisolated Service Preload
nodes.rationale: Service preloads run with contextIsolation:false, sandbox:false, nodeIntegration:false because a context-isolated preload cannot wrap window.Notification — Ferdium's proven model for these exact services; the shell renderer keeps full context isolation.

nodes.label: Graphite Minimal Design System
nodes.rationale: Dark-first neutral surfaces with a single accent so the shell stays quiet and doesn't clash with embedded services' own UIs; rejected native vibrancy/Mica (finicky in Electron, two styling targets) and expressive/colorful direction. All text pairs meet WCAG AA.

nodes.label: Viber Exclusion
nodes.rationale: Viber has no web client at all (its desktop app is a native QR-paired client with nothing embeddable) and no ferdium recipe exists, so it is deliberately excluded from the five-service set.

nodes.label: ShellState Broadcast Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Main process is the single source of truth: it holds settings + runtime state and broadcasts a full ShellState snapshot to the renderer over typed IPC on every mutation; broadcast() is the single place where state fans out to rail badges, dock/overlay badges, and tray tooltip.

nodes.label: Tag-Push Release Flow
nodes.rationale: v* tag push -> matrix build -> GitHub Release with installers attached via softprops/action-gh-release. Rejected electron-builder built-in publishing (publish: github would leak publish behavior into local builds and produce draft releases with less control) and build-only artifacts (users would have to dig into Actions runs — fails the 'download directly' requirement).

nodes.label: Unsigned Builds Decision
nodes.rationale: No signing certificates exist; CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=false skips mac signing cleanly in CI. Users bypass Gatekeeper (right-click -> Open) and SmartScreen (More info -> Run anyway) manually. Code signing/notarization deferred until distribution widens.

nodes.label: Version/Tag Match Guard
nodes.rationale: On tag runs, fail the build before packaging if the pushed tag does not equal 'v' + package.json version, so releases can never carry a mismatched version.

nodes.label: publish: null Policy
nodes.rationale: electron-builder.yml keeps publish: null so local packaging never publishes; CI additionally passes --publish never as belt-and-braces because electron-builder can auto-publish on CI tag builds when a token is present.

nodes.label: pnpm allowBuilds allowlist
nodes.rationale: Only electron, electron-winstaller, and esbuild are allowed to run install-time build scripts under pnpm's script-blocking policy.

nodes.label: Goetia App Icon (glowing timer/orbit ring on dark squircle)
nodes.norm_label: goetia app icon (glowing timer/orbit ring on dark squircle)

nodes.norm_label: progress/timer ring motif (yellow-to-red gradient arc dissolving into dots around a central glowing dot)

nodes.label: macOS-style Dark Squircle App Icon Design
nodes.norm_label: macos-style dark squircle app icon design

nodes.label: Core Radial Gradient (white-hot to ember orange)
nodes.norm_label: core radial gradient (white-hot to ember orange)

nodes.label: macOS Tray Template Icon @2x (monochrome ring-and-dot glyph, Retina)
nodes.norm_label: macos tray template icon @2x (monochrome ring-and-dot glyph, retina)

nodes.label: macOS Template Image Convention (monochrome icon auto-tinted by menu bar theme)
nodes.norm_label: macos template image convention (monochrome icon auto-tinted by menu bar theme)

nodes.label: NOTE: backgroundThrottling stays ON by default — disabling it also
nodes.norm_label: note: backgroundthrottling stays on by default — disabling it also

nodes.label: Goetia features & verification inventory
nodes.rationale: Doubles as a regression checklist: every listed behaviour must still hold after any change. 'Verified' means an automated test asserts it; 'Manual' means no automated coverage exists.

nodes.label: One window, many services (WebContentsView per service)
nodes.rationale: Each service gets its own WebContentsView on an isolated persist:<id> session so cookies/logins never mix between services.
nodes.norm_label: one window, many services (webcontentsview per service)

nodes.label: Per-service unread counts from recipes
nodes.rationale: Recipes extract counts every ~2s; the HTML fixtures in tests/fixtures are the oracle for the expected number.

nodes.label: Stale indicator (grey dot when a recipe throws)
nodes.rationale: Reported once per transition into stale, not per tick, to avoid a broadcast storm.
nodes.norm_label: stale indicator (grey dot when a recipe throws)

nodes.label: Native OS notifications with per-service icons
nodes.norm_label: native os notifications with per-service icons

nodes.label: Synthetic notifications for pages that never notify
nodes.rationale: Messenger never fires in-page Notifications, so the runner synthesises one when the unread count rises and the doc is unfocused.
nodes.norm_label: synthetic notifications for pages that never notify

nodes.label: Notification shim (page Notification API rerouted to native)
nodes.norm_label: notification shim (page notification api rerouted to native)

nodes.label: Crash resilience with backoff and a reload cap
nodes.rationale: Auto-reload is capped at 5 and the count is only forgotten after a stable-uptime dwell, so a load-crash-reload loop cannot reset the cap forever.
nodes.norm_label: crash resilience with backoff and a reload cap

nodes.label: Hibernation of idle services
nodes.rationale: Config-gated and off by default: freeing a view drops the live session state most chat services rely on.

nodes.label: Keep-alive trusted clicks
nodes.rationale: Zalo and Shopee unmount their chat widget without user interaction; page-JS synthetic clicks are untrusted, so main dispatches a real input event and the deferred hide is guarded against a destroyed view.

nodes.label: Visibility spoof (Zalo)
nodes.rationale: Pins visibilityState=visible so a hidden view keeps its socket and DOM alive.

nodes.label: New-service reconciliation in settings normalize
nodes.rationale: A service added after settings.json was written appears disabled by default without losing existing prefs.

nodes.label: Corrupt settings.json tolerance
nodes.rationale: A malformed file is coerced to defaults per field instead of bricking startup.

nodes.label: IPC sender policy (shell-only vs service channels)
nodes.norm_label: ipc sender policy (shell-only vs service channels)

nodes.label: External-link allowlist (only http(s) reach the OS browser)
nodes.norm_label: external-link allowlist (only http(s) reach the os browser)

nodes.label: Permission origin check (camera/mic/notifications)
nodes.rationale: A service may only be granted permissions for its own origin, so a redirected or framed foreign page inherits nothing.

nodes.label: Navigation allowlist (helper exists, guard not wired)
nodes.rationale: Known limit: the will-navigate guard is deliberately not attached to service views until each service's real login redirects are verified live, because a wrong allowlist would break sign-in.
nodes.norm_label: navigation allowlist (helper exists, guard not wired)

nodes.label: Regression: service switch not broadcast after setRuntime no-op guard
nodes.rationale: activateService relied on setRuntime(id,{hibernated:false}) to broadcast; the new no-op guard skips the broadcast when nothing changes, so a non-hibernated service produced no shell:state update. Fix: activate.ts calls ctx.state.touch() explicitly.
nodes.norm_label: regression: service switch not broadcast after setruntime no-op guard

nodes.label: Notification service icons implementation plan
nodes.rationale: Goal: a brand-coloured service tile in every OS banner so services are distinguishable without reading the text.

nodes.label: Build-time tile rasterisation pipeline
nodes.rationale: A script rasterises one tile per service into committed PNGs at build time so no image is ever decoded into or retained by the running app, and @resvg/resvg-js stays a devDependency — nothing new enters the runtime or packaging dependency graph. Canvas 128px, radius ratio 0.34, glyph ratio 0.56, macOS inset 28/38 derived from constants.

nodes.label: iconFileName(id, platform)
nodes.rationale: macOS gets the padded <id>-mac.png variant so the tile reads smaller than the app icon in the banner slot; every other platform gets the full-bleed <id>.png.

nodes.label: resolveIcons(dir, ids, platform, exists)
nodes.rationale: Resolved once at startup with an injected exists() probe: a missing asset silently drops out of the map rather than costing a stat call on every notification, and the injection keeps the helper pure/testable.

nodes.label: notificationTitle(raw, fallback)
nodes.rationale: With the '— <Service>' suffix dropped, the title carries the sender alone, so a recipe reporting an empty title would raise a headless banner; fall back to the service name.

nodes.label: NotificationRouter.handle wiring
nodes.rationale: Thin wiring only — the shouldNotify mute gate stays first in handle, ahead of any icon work; pure decisions live in src/main/lib helpers that carry the unit tests. Electron's Notification cannot be exercised under Vitest, so banner behaviour is verified by hand.

nodes.label: Ship notification icons via extraResources (outside the asar)
nodes.rationale: extraResources drops the PNGs beside the asar in Contents/Resources so the OS can open the path; a file inside app.asar is not an OS-openable path. Matches the app.isPackaged branch that points at process.resourcesPath.
nodes.norm_label: ship notification icons via extraresources (outside the asar)

nodes.label: NativeImage icon fallback for Electron 43 on darwin
nodes.rationale: Electron 43 may only honour `icon` as a NativeImage on darwin; if the path form draws nothing, create the image with nativeImage.createFromPath and record it in the commit message so the next person does not 'simplify' it back.
nodes.norm_label: nativeimage icon fallback for electron 43 on darwin

nodes.label: Service loading screen (waking overlay) implementation plan
nodes.rationale: Cover every service load (cold start, hibernation wake, reload, crash retry) until the chat UI is actually usable, with a 10s reveal fallback.
nodes.norm_label: service loading screen (waking overlay) implementation plan

nodes.label: ServiceRuntime.waking flag
nodes.rationale: One per-service boolean in shared runtime state is the single source of truth the overlay view and the rail tiles both read, so cover and tile animation can never disagree.

nodes.label: ServiceMeta.waitForReady
nodes.rationale: Marks services whose chat renders long after did-finish-load, so load completion must not clear the cover. A test asserts the flag matches exactly the recipes that define ready(), preventing drift between the two tables.

nodes.label: Recipe.ready(doc) chat-usable check
nodes.rationale: A DOM predicate per service (Messenger: chat rows rendered; Shopee: mini-chat expanded, i.e. the keep-alive click landed) that ends the cover early. Absent means did-finish-load is the ready signal instead.

nodes.label: startReadyPoll in the service preload
nodes.rationale: Polls ready() every 250ms, reports service:ready exactly once per document, then stops. A throwing ready() counts as not-ready because main's reveal timeout is the backstop — the page can never stay covered forever.

nodes.label: endsWake(event, meta) reveal rule
nodes.rationale: load-finished reveals only services without a ready() check; every other end event (recipe-ready, timeout, crashed, load-failed, destroyed) always reveals, so the cover can never outlive its view or trap a Retry button underneath.

nodes.label: WakingTracker
nodes.rationale: Owns one timeout per service; begin() re-arms the clock so a reload mid-wake restarts it, and end() disarms it so no stray timer touches state after the reveal.

nodes.label: WAKE_TIMEOUT_MS reveal backstop (10s)
nodes.rationale: A logged-out page or captcha never satisfies ready(), so a hard 10s timeout guarantees the user always gets the page back.

nodes.label: LoadingOverlay WebContentsView
nodes.rationale: One app-owned view stacked above the active service view, kept contextIsolation:true/sandbox:true. show() re-adds it at the top of the z-order every call so it stays above a freshly re-activated service view; it is loaded hidden at startup and carries its own background colour so no white flash appears before the page paints. The service page stays visible and interactive underneath so keep-alive trusted clicks still work.

nodes.label: syncOverlay visibility rule in broadcast()
nodes.rationale: Shows the cover only when the active service is waking and not crashed, and hides it while the quick switcher or settings panel is open so the overlay never sits on top of shell UI.

nodes.label: tile-breathe rail animation
nodes.rationale: Background services waking during startup have no visible cover, so the rail tile breathes instead. The prefers-reduced-motion kill-switch in tokens.css must stay last so it wins.

nodes.label: Ember Portal loading page (second renderer entry)
nodes.rationale: loading.html is a second multi-page renderer entry with its own sandboxed preload bridge (window.goetiaLoading.onState); main re-sends the last state on did-finish-load in case update() raced the page load.
nodes.norm_label: ember portal loading page (second renderer entry)

nodes.label: Shopee chat-focus implementation plan
nodes.rationale: Render the embedded Shopee service as the buyer mini-chat full-window — no shopping chrome, real unread counts, auto-open of the collapsed widget, disabled by default.

nodes.label: Shopee entry URL moved to the homepage
nodes.rationale: Never target /webchat — it hits Shopee's anti-bot wall (verify/captcha, scene=crawler_item). Buyer chat lives in the mini-chat widget on the shopping site instead.
nodes.norm_label: shopee entry url moved to the homepage

nodes.label: Structural-selectors-only rule for Shopee
nodes.rationale: Shopee's class names are build-hashed (e.g. UvGSSkd1qQ) and change on every deploy, so the recipe keys only on the stable ids #main and #shopee-mini-chat-embedded plus child positions.

nodes.label: chatHeader(doc) helper
nodes.rationale: Returns the header row when expanded and the whole wrapper when collapsed — the one place the unread badge text lives in either state.

nodes.label: shopee.count(doc)
nodes.rationale: Parses the first digits out of the widget badge, falling back to the document title when the host is absent; must never throw and must return zero on blank.html.

nodes.label: shopee.keepAlive(doc)
nodes.rationale: The collapsed pill needs a trusted click to open — page-JS synthetic clicks are untrusted (same machinery as Zalo's activation modal). Returns null when already expanded, and skips a laid-out-but-tiny rect because that means the view is not really laid out yet. The runner rate-limits to one click per 30s.

nodes.label: Shopee chat-focus CSS (expanded-state gated)
nodes.rationale: Every rule is gated on the expanded state via :has(> div > div:nth-child(2)). Ungated rules stretched the collapsed pill into a blank view and would have hidden a captcha, so while collapsed the page must stay untouched and the pill keeps its real rect for keepAlive. Hiding (not removing) keeps textContent readable for count().

nodes.label: Shopee disabled by default
nodes.rationale: DEFAULT_SETTINGS.disabled.shopee = true, so the default rail shows only messenger and zalo; the e2e rail-count assertion is the guard.

nodes.label: Code signing and notarization — parked decision record
nodes.rationale: Not started, blocked on paid developer enrollments, so it is a decision record rather than an executable plan. Only the macOS half is worth doing first: it is cheaper (USD 99/yr vs 200-400/yr) and fixes the recurring keychain prompt.
nodes.norm_label: code signing and notarization — parked decision record

nodes.label: Code-signing designated requirement (DR)
nodes.rationale: A keychain item's ACL trusts the creating app by its DR. Under ad-hoc signing there is no team identity so the DR collapses to the binary's own cdhash; a Developer ID signature yields a DR anchored on the team identifier that is stable across every future build.

nodes.label: Recurring 'Goetia Safe Storage' keychain prompt
nodes.rationale: enableCookieEncryption stores the Chromium cookie key in the login keychain; every rebuild changes the cdhash, so the next launch is a different program asking for someone else's item and macOS prompts. 'Always Allow' only pins that one build. Turning the fuse off is not an option — Chromium would fall back to a hardcoded key, leaving every service's session cookies readable on disk.

nodes.label: Developer ID signing + notarization (macOS steps)
nodes.rationale: Drop identity:'-' so electron-builder auto-discovers the cert and add mac.notarize.teamId. Keep hardenedRuntime and the entitlements exactly as they are — notarization rejects allow-dyld-environment-variables, which is already banned; do not add it to get past a failure.

nodes.label: Open question: fuse flipping vs signing order
nodes.rationale: resetAdHocDarwinSignature exists because flipping fuses invalidates the signature and macOS refuses Notification Center registration for an unsigned bundle. With a real identity the flag should become false so the ad-hoc re-sign cannot land on top of the Developer ID signature — but electron-builder's fuse/sign step ordering must be confirmed empirically, not assumed. enableEmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation also interacts with post-signing asar modification.
nodes.norm_label: open question: fuse flipping vs signing order

nodes.label: macOS Gatekeeper 'damaged' quarantine gate
nodes.rationale: Downloaded dmgs are quarantined; users clear it once with xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine, notarization removes it entirely.

nodes.label: Windows SmartScreen gate
nodes.rationale: An OV certificate still needs reputation to accumulate before SmartScreen goes quiet; EV clears it immediately but costs more.

nodes.label: CI signing secrets migration
nodes.rationale: release.yml forces CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY:false because no signing material exists; when certificates land, replace it with repository secrets and remove the flag from the macOS job only.

nodes.label: Reliability & performance remediation plan
nodes.rationale: Fixes a window-lifecycle crash, a defeated crash-reload cap, unbounded background polling, a broadcast storm, resize thrash, a startup brick and several leaks. Decision logic moves into pure helpers with vitest tests; index.ts/tray.ts/views.ts stay thin wiring. Task 4 must land before Task 11 because the timeout path relies on the stale dedup.

nodes.label: Close-to-tray off must quit, not zombie the app
nodes.rationale: With close-to-tray off the X button means quit — never leave a destroyed-window process running with live timers and tray behind it. broadcast() early-returns on win.isDestroyed() so nothing touches the dead window.
nodes.norm_label: close-to-tray off must quit, not zombie the app

nodes.label: ResilienceManager DWELL_MS crash-count dwell
nodes.rationale: noteRecovered used to reset the attempt count on every did-finish-load, so a load-crash-reload loop reset MAX_AUTO_RELOADS every cycle and reloaded forever. The count is now forgotten only after the page stays up for DWELL_MS (30s); a crash within the dwell clears the timer and keeps the count.

nodes.label: READY_POLL_MAX_ATTEMPTS bound
nodes.rationale: Once main's 10s reveal timeout has surely fired a later ready() cannot re-cover the current load, so polling on forever at a login wall only burns CPU. Cap = ceil(10000/interval) + 4 buffer ticks.

nodes.label: Runner stale dedup (report on transition only)
nodes.rationale: A logged-out page throws on every ~2s tick; reporting stale each time produced a broadcast storm. A module-local flag reports only on the transition into stale, and a successful count re-arms it.
nodes.norm_label: runner stale dedup (report on transition only)

nodes.label: setRuntime no-op guard (isNoOp)
nodes.rationale: An identical patch no longer calls touch(), so repeated {stale:true} stops broadcasting; unread is compared field-wise because it is a nested object.

nodes.label: scheduleLayout resize coalescing
nodes.rationale: A burst of resize events collapses into one layout pass per ~16ms tick instead of one setBounds sweep per event.

nodes.label: Single-pass Messenger unread detection
nodes.rationale: isUnreadRow now reads getComputedStyle once per element in one traversal instead of two overlapping querySelectorAll sweeps. Behaviour-preserving: the fixture count of 3 is the guard. The blue-dominant colour test excludes the green presence dot.

nodes.label: settings normalize per-field coercion
nodes.rationale: A hand-mangled settings.json (order not an array, record fields not objects) used to throw at startup and brick the app; each field is now coerced back to its default independently.

nodes.label: connectShell returns its unsubscribe
nodes.rationale: Returning the unsubscribe makes React register it as the useEffect cleanup automatically, so a shell reload does not stack duplicate shell:state handlers — App.tsx needs no edit.

nodes.label: Guarded deferred trustedClick visibility toggle
nodes.rationale: The 300ms setVisible(false) could fire after the view was destroyed ('Object has been destroyed'); the timer is now tracked per service, guarded by !webContents.isDestroyed(), and cancelled in destroy().

nodes.label: COUNT_TIMEOUT_MS hung-tick race
nodes.rationale: A count() that never settles wedged the busy guard so no further tick ever ran. Racing count() against an 8s rejection lets the existing catch report stale and finally release busy.

nodes.label: Consolidated badgeLabel (99+ threshold)
nodes.rationale: One shared label with a single 99+ cap replaces the duplicate local badgeText in ServiceTile (which capped at 9+), so rail tile, quick switcher and taskbar overlay agree.

nodes.label: Security hardening implementation plan
nodes.rationale: Hardens against local malware (threat A), hostile service pages (threat B) and a tampered supply chain (threat C). Service views must keep contextIsolation:false / sandbox:false for the recipe workarounds, so hardening works around that rather than flipping it; the shell window's isolation is never weakened.

nodes.label: electronFuses block in electron-builder.yml
nodes.rationale: Closes the run-as-node / NODE_OPTIONS / --inspect code-exec paths, encrypts session cookies via the OS keychain instead of plaintext SQLite, and makes the integrity-checked asar the only load source. Keys are schema-validated: enableRunAsNode is NOT valid (only runAsNode) and a bad key fails the whole config. resetAdHocDarwinSignature keeps the binary ad-hoc signed after fuse-flipping, which Notification Center registration depends on.

nodes.label: isSafeExternalUrl scheme allowlist
nodes.rationale: Only web schemes may be handed to the OS; file:/smb:/javascript: and custom schemes from a hostile page's window.open are dropped, and a malformed URL is rejected by the try/catch rather than throwing into the handler.

nodes.label: permissionAllowed origin check
nodes.rationale: Grants only notifications and media, and only when the requesting origin equals the service's own origin — a page navigated or redirected elsewhere gets nothing. Wired into both setPermissionRequestHandler and setPermissionCheckHandler so a check cannot bypass the request path.

nodes.label: ipcSenderAllowed sender-origin policy
nodes.rationale: Shell-only channels must come from the shell frame; service channels must come from the frame of the very service named in the payload, so a compromised service page can neither drive shell settings nor spoof another service's id. An unknown frame is always rejected.

nodes.label: SHELL_ONLY_CHANNELS classification
nodes.rationale: Every renderer→main channel is classified once in shared/ipc.ts: shell-only, or a service channel carrying its own serviceId. New channels must join one of the two sets.

nodes.label: register() IPC dispatcher wrapper
nodes.rationale: A single wrapper resolves fromShell and the sender's serviceId, then silently drops spoofed or cross-service messages — every existing on(...) call site stays unchanged, so no handler can forget the check.

nodes.label: ServiceViewManager.serviceIdForWebContentsId
nodes.rationale: Maps a sending webContents id back to the service that owns the view — the frame→service lookup the IPC policy needs to detect id spoofing.

nodes.label: NotificationThrottle per-service rate limit
nodes.rationale: An 800ms floor between native banners per service, so a hostile page (or a runaway recipe) using the Notification shim cannot spam the OS notification centre. Services are tracked independently.

nodes.label: isNavigationAllowed navigation containment
nodes.rationale: A blocked will-navigate/will-redirect is preventDefault'ed and re-opened in the OS browser, so a phishing redirect never loads inside the app with the recipe preload attached.

nodes.label: ALLOWED_HOSTS per-service allowlist
nodes.rationale: Each service's own domain plus the hosts its login flow bounces through. The list is a starting set only — this is the one task explicitly gated on live login verification per service, because a missing auth host silently breaks sign-in and unit tests cannot catch it.

nodes.label: Supply chain: SHA-pinned actions + build provenance attestation
nodes.rationale: Mutable major tags let an upstream compromise reach the release build, so every uses: is pinned to a commit SHA with the tag kept as a comment, and attest-build-provenance signs the dmg/exe (needs id-token and attestations write permissions).
nodes.norm_label: supply chain: sha-pinned actions + build provenance attestation

nodes.label: Tightened renderer CSP (object/base/frame locks)
nodes.rationale: Both privileged renderer pages deny plugins, base-tag hijack and framing; they load only first-party assets so the tighter policy changes nothing functional.

nodes.label: Goetia engineering guardrails
nodes.rationale: Invariants distilled from the 2026-08-07 review and security audit; breaking one is a regression even if tests pass.

nodes.label: Definition of done (lint, typecheck, test, e2e, real package build)
nodes.rationale: Packaging changes need a real package:mac build that launches because config-only verification cannot prove the app still starts.
nodes.norm_label: definition of done (lint, typecheck, test, e2e, real package build)

nodes.label: Process boundaries: sandboxed shell, unsandboxed service views
nodes.rationale: Service views must run contextIsolation:false + sandbox:false for the recipe workarounds, so isolation is never relied on there; harden around it instead and never add nodeIntegration.
nodes.norm_label: process boundaries: sandboxed shell, unsandboxed service views

nodes.label: src/shared stays process-agnostic
nodes.rationale: No electron and no DOM imports so the module is safe to bundle into both main and the sandboxed preload.

nodes.label: Pure decision logic lives in lib/ helpers
nodes.rationale: Keeps views.ts / index.ts / ipc-handlers.ts thin wiring so behaviour is unit-testable without Electron.
nodes.norm_label: pure decision logic lives in lib/ helpers

nodes.label: Electron fuses invariant (electron-builder.yml)
nodes.rationale: Keys are schema-checked: enableRunAsNode is not a valid key and a bad key fails the whole config with 'electronFuses should be one of these: null'.

nodes.label: build/entitlements.mac.plist minimal entitlement set
nodes.rationale: Never add allow-dyld-environment-variables — it reopens the injection path the fuses close.

nodes.label: IPC register() wrapper enforcing ipcSenderAllowed
nodes.rationale: Never act on an attacker-controllable payload (persist settings, spawn, navigate) without a sender check.

nodes.label: SHELL_ONLY_CHANNELS channel classification
nodes.rationale: Every new channel must be classified: shell-only (only the shell frame may send) or service channel carrying a serviceId validated against the sending frame.

nodes.label: isSafeExternalUrl external-link gate
nodes.rationale: shell.openExternal only for web schemes, so a hostile page cannot hand file:/smb:/custom schemes to the OS.

nodes.label: permissionAllowed origin-checked permission grant
nodes.rationale: Grants only notifications + media; broadening the allowlist or dropping the origin check hands camera/mic to any embedded origin.

nodes.label: isNavigationAllowed / ALLOWED_HOSTS navigation containment
nodes.rationale: The will-navigate/will-redirect guard is deliberately NOT yet wired into views.ts: each service's real auth-redirect hosts must be added and a live login verified first, or containment locks users out.

nodes.label: NotificationRouter with per-service NotificationThrottle
nodes.rationale: Single rate-limited path; a second unthrottled path would let a hostile page spam native banners via the Notification shim.

nodes.label: Renderer CSP invariant for index.html and loading.html
nodes.rationale: default-src 'self' plus object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-src 'none'; no remote assets and no innerHTML in the shell.
nodes.norm_label: renderer csp invariant for index.html and loading.html

nodes.label: count(doc) must be cheap and always settle
nodes.rationale: Recipe polling runs at the full intervalMs even while hidden (websockets exempt the page from Chromium throttling), so per-tick cost is paid 24/7; no getComputedStyle/getBoundingClientRect sweeps, no full IndexedDB getAll, and never return a promise that can never settle.
nodes.norm_label: count(doc) must be cheap and always settle

nodes.label: Report on change only (runner dedup + setRuntime no-op skip)
nodes.rationale: Per-tick broadcasts cause a full ShellState broadcast and React re-render every tick for a persistently failing recipe.
nodes.norm_label: report on change only (runner dedup + setruntime no-op skip)

nodes.label: Bounded timers and listener teardown
nodes.rationale: Every interval/timeout/listener is cleared on destroy() and quit; deferred callbacks guard on !webContents.isDestroyed(); polls stay capped like READY_POLL_MAX_ATTEMPTS.

nodes.label: ResilienceManager crash-count dwell
nodes.rationale: Forget a crash count only after DWELL_MS uptime; resetting on every did-finish-load defeats the auto-reload cap.

nodes.label: scheduleLayout() resize coalescing
nodes.rationale: Re-bounding every view per resize event is heavy work on a hot event stream.

nodes.label: One long-lived window lifecycle assumption
nodes.rationale: With close-to-tray off the window is destroyed and the app quits, so broadcast() and tray handlers must be guarded by win.isDestroyed().

nodes.label: Adding a service checklist
nodes.rationale: Six coupled edits (ServiceId/SERVICES, DEFAULT_SETTINGS records, recipe, fixture+test row, ALLOWED_HOSTS, notification icons) that silently rot if done partially.

nodes.label: Ad-hoc signed packaging and fuse verification
nodes.rationale: Read fuses from the packaged app via @electron/fuses getCurrentFuseWire (byte 49='1'/on, 48='0'/off) because the CLI is not on PATH; require it from node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/@electron/fuses.
nodes.norm_label: ad-hoc signed packaging and fuse verification

nodes.label: Goetia Safe Storage keychain re-prompt per build
nodes.rationale: Ad-hoc signing makes each build's designated requirement its own cdhash, so every rebuild looks like a new app to macOS; answer Always Allow and never disable enableCookieEncryption to silence it.
nodes.norm_label: goetia safe storage keychain re-prompt per build

nodes.label: Goetia multi-service chat client
nodes.rationale: Electron + TypeScript + React, local-only: no server, no accounts, no telemetry; macOS and Windows only. Viber is intentionally absent because it has no embeddable web client.

nodes.label: Unsigned-app first-launch gate (Gatekeeper / SmartScreen)
nodes.rationale: Only downloaded copies carry the quarantine flag; a locally built app opens with no warning. Cleared once with xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine, or 'More info → Run anyway' on Windows.

nodes.label: Goetia Safe Storage keychain prompt (user-facing)
nodes.rationale: Clicking Deny leaves saved logins locked and forces a re-login to every service; deleting the generic password silences the prompt but discards every saved session.

nodes.label: Per-service unread-count recipes (src/preload/recipes/)
nodes.rationale: Selector + fixture are fixed together because pnpm test locks them to each other; a site redesign breaks only the badge, never chatting.

nodes.label: Stale-count dot on a service tile
nodes.rationale: Surfaces 'the counter needs an update' rather than pretending zero unread.
nodes.norm_label: stale-count dot on a service tile

nodes.label: Isolated persist:<id> session per service
nodes.rationale: Each account stays logged in independently across restarts, stored under ~/Library/Application Support/Goetia.

nodes.label: Close-to-tray background running
nodes.rationale: Closing the window keeps the app in the menu bar/tray so notifications still arrive; quitting is explicit.

nodes.label: Ember Portal branding and icon sources
nodes.rationale: A summoning circle as pure energy matching the ember accent (dark #FF9E2C, light #E8590C); SVG sources in resources/, PNGs regenerated with rsvg-convert.
nodes.norm_label: ember portal branding and icon sources

nodes.label: corepack pnpm invocation workflow
nodes.rationale: pnpm may not be on PATH with Node via Homebrew; the version is pinned in package.json packageManager, and tools that spawn pnpm themselves (electron-builder) need the shims on PATH.

nodes.label: Release cut by pushing a version tag
nodes.rationale: The tag must match package.json's version.
nodes.norm_label: release cut by pushing a version tag

nodes.label: Top-bar service rail with configurable menu position
nodes.rationale: Default is a top bar because each chat app already has its own left-hand column, so a second left rail would double up.
nodes.norm_label: top-bar service rail with configurable menu position

nodes.label: Notification service icons design
nodes.rationale: Goal: tell one service from another in the OS notification banner without reading it.

nodes.label: We do not own the banner layout
nodes.rationale: macOS fixes the app icon, timestamp, and attachment slots; the only controllable dimension is how much of the attachment box the artwork fills, via transparent padding baked into the PNG. Every other decision follows from that.
nodes.norm_label: we do not own the banner layout

nodes.label: Placement decision: native Notification.icon
nodes.rationale: Electron's icon maps to UNNotificationAttachment on darwin and the toast appLogoOverride on win32; a file path is passed so no NativeImage is retained in main.

nodes.label: Brand-colour tile with white glyph artwork
nodes.rationale: A bare white glyph is invisible against a macOS light-mode banner; a composite app+service image would show the app icon twice on macOS.
nodes.norm_label: brand-colour tile with white glyph artwork

nodes.label: scripts/build-notification-icons.mjs
nodes.rationale: Reads SERVICES from src/shared/services.ts directly (Node 26 imports TypeScript) so there is no duplicated service table and no drift; rasterises with @resvg/resvg-js as a devDependency only.

nodes.label: resources/notification-icons/*.png committed variants
nodes.rationale: Committed rather than generated at build time so neither a normal build nor electron-builder needs the rasteriser installed; two variants per service (<id>.png full-bleed for Windows, <id>-mac.png inset).

nodes.label: MAC_INSET_RATIO (28/38) named geometry constants
nodes.rationale: Ratios derived from ServiceTile (11px radius and 18px glyph on a 32px tile) rather than hardcoded pixels; padding is the only lever over the macOS attachment box, and full-bleed on Windows because there the tile IS the app-icon slot.

nodes.label: iconFileName(id, platform)
nodes.rationale: Returns the -mac variant on darwin and the plain one otherwise.

nodes.label: resolveIcons(dir, ids, platform, exists)
nodes.rationale: exists is injected so the resolver is testable without touching the filesystem; a missing file is silently omitted rather than throwing.

nodes.label: notificationTitle(raw, fallback)
nodes.rationale: Dropping the '— <Service>' suffix removed the guarantee that a title is never blank, so an empty sender falls back to the service name instead of a headless banner.

nodes.label: extraResources icon placement (asarUnpack rejected)
nodes.rationale: asarUnpack leaves an app.asar/... path only Node's patched fs can resolve, which native notification code cannot open; extraResources lands the PNGs at process.resourcesPath, a real path on disk. The files: exclusion stops them also being packed into the asar.

nodes.label: NotificationRouter constructor-time icon map
nodes.rationale: SERVICES.length existsSync calls once at startup and none on the notification path; the shouldNotify gate stays ahead of any icon work so muting still costs nothing.

nodes.label: Every service has both PNG variants on disk (test)
nodes.rationale: The test that earns its keep: adding a sixth service without re-running pnpm run icons fails the suite instead of shipping a blank slot.
nodes.norm_label: every service has both png variants on disk (test)

nodes.label: Rejected: custom frameless banner window
nodes.rationale: Full layout control, but forfeits Do Not Disturb, Notification Center history, OS grouping and multi-display placement, and adds another window to own.

nodes.label: Service loading screen (waking overlay) design
nodes.rationale: Activating a service showed the raw page mid-load (Messenger's Facebook header flash, Shopee's shopping homepage), so every load is hidden behind a branded screen until chat is usable.

nodes.label: ServiceRuntime.waking flag
nodes.rationale: Set true on view creation and did-start-loading (SPA-internal navigation does not fire it, so no spurious overlay mid-use); cleared by the first of service:ready, did-finish-load for services without waitForReady, the 10 s timeout, crash/failed load, or view destruction — the last case prevents eternally-breathing tiles.

nodes.label: src/main/lib/waking-rules.ts
nodes.rationale: Pure transition module in the same pattern as hibernation-rules.ts so the state machine is unit-testable with fake timers.

nodes.label: Recipe.ready?(doc): boolean
nodes.rationale: did-finish-load fires long before chat is usable on SPA services, so readiness is per-recipe; ready() throwing counts as not-ready and the timeout still resolves it.

nodes.label: ServiceMeta.waitForReady flag
nodes.rationale: Tells main that did-finish-load must not clear waking for messenger/shopee; a unit test asserts the flag matches which recipes define ready() so the two cannot drift.

nodes.label: service:ready IPC channel
nodes.rationale: Renderer→main channel carrying serviceId; the service preload polls ready() every 250 ms after DOMContentLoaded and sends it once, then stops.

nodes.label: 10 s timeout reveal fallback
nodes.rationale: Login walls, captchas, and Shopee's anti-bot page can never signal ready, so the page is revealed as-is after 10 s: a partial page beats trapping the user behind a spinner, and drifted ready selectors degrade to this instead of a lockout.

nodes.label: src/main/loading-overlay.ts overlay WebContentsView
nodes.rationale: One view created hidden at startup and preloaded so showing it is instant with no white flash; shown by re-adding at the top of the z-order and bounded by the shared viewBounds. Visible iff the active service is waking && !crashed and neither Settings nor the Quick Switcher is open.

nodes.label: Synthetic input does not reach invisible views
nodes.rationale: trustedClick() flashes hidden views visible to work around this, and Shopee's readiness depends on that click — so the loading cover must stack above a still-visible view rather than hide it (a 300 ms reveal flash would defeat the feature), and an in-page veil was rejected because it lives in hostile third-party DOM and must survive redirects.
nodes.norm_label: synthetic input does not reach invisible views

nodes.label: Ember Portal overlay animation
nodes.rationale: The app icon decomposes naturally into a spinning fire ring (~2 s/turn) and a breathing core orb (~2.4 s), over --bg-0 following the resolved theme, with a 'Waking {Service}…' caption; the global prefers-reduced-motion rule disables it.

nodes.label: loading.html second renderer entry
nodes.rationale: Plain TS, no React — one static SVG, CSS animations, one IPC listener updating caption and data-theme; reuses tokens.css.

nodes.label: ServiceTile breathes while waking
nodes.rationale: Rail feedback for background wakes the overlay cannot show; crash/stale dots and badges still render on top.

nodes.label: messenger.ready(): chat list rows exist
nodes.rationale: doc.querySelectorAll("a[href*='/t/']").length > 0 — by then the recipe CSS has long since hidden the Facebook banner, so no header flash is visible.

nodes.label: shopee.ready(): mini-chat expanded
nodes.rationale: The #shopee-mini-chat-embedded wrapper has both header and body children — the same structural check as chatHeader(), i.e. the keep-alive click already worked.

nodes.label: Shopee chat-focus design
nodes.rationale: Shopee shipped as a basic /webchat embed; live verification found an anti-bot wall and a shopping-homepage-first view, so chat is made to fill the view like every other service.

nodes.label: Shopee anti-bot captcha wall
nodes.rationale: /webchat trips shopee.vn/verify/captcha?...scene=crawler_item on every launch and repeated hits risk flagging the account; the design therefore avoids /webchat, automated navigation, and request blocking, leaving one rate-limited trusted click as the only synthetic input.

nodes.label: Entry URL decision: https://shopee.vn/
nodes.rationale: The homepage is the supported entry that loads clean in a real logged-in session, and it makes reload robustness free: the preload re-injects recipe CSS on every DOMContentLoaded and reload lands back on the homepage.

nodes.label: Chat-focus recipe CSS (hide #main, fix host to inset 0)
nodes.rationale: Only the stable IDs #main and #shopee-mini-chat-embedded are referenced — every class below them is build-hashed (e.g. UvGSSkd1qQ) and must not be used; the expanded header is hidden because its expand button navigates to /webchat.
nodes.norm_label: chat-focus recipe css (hide #main, fix host to inset 0)

nodes.label: :has() expanded-state gating of every CSS rule
nodes.rationale: Live testing showed ungated rules stretch the collapsed pill into a blank white view and would invisibly hide a captcha; gating leaves login and captcha pages untouched and preserves the pill's real rect for keepAlive.
nodes.norm_label: :has() expanded-state gating of every css rule

nodes.label: keepAlive auto-open of the collapsed pill
nodes.rationale: Returns the pill element's center (not the host, which may be restyled), reusing the Zalo trusted-click machinery rate-limited to one click per 30 s; must survive happy-dom's zero rects via the zalo degenerate-rect guard.
nodes.norm_label: keepalive auto-open of the collapsed pill

nodes.label: Shopee unread count from host textContent
nodes.rationale: Parses the first integer in the header/pill textContent because Shopee titles never carry '(n)'; display:none keeps textContent readable, and it falls back to 0 when the badge is absent.
nodes.norm_label: shopee unread count from host textcontent

nodes.label: Shopee disabled by default
nodes.rationale: User decision: Shopee is opt-in, enabled once in Settings; services/settings/e2e expectations revert accordingly.

nodes.label: No webRequest network filtering for Shopee
nodes.rationale: Blocking makes the client look more bot-like to a platform that already served a captcha and risks breaking login; the hidden shopping shell loads once and idles.
nodes.norm_label: no webrequest network filtering for shopee

nodes.label: tests/fixtures/shopee.html structural fixture
nodes.rationale: Rebuilt from the real structure with hashed class names replaced by neutral ones — the fixture stays honest because every selector is structural; a collapsed-state fixture locks keepAlive's pill detection and its null return when expanded.

nodes.label: Hardening & remediation design
nodes.rationale: Records every accepted finding from two code reviews plus a defensive security audit, the fix decision for each, and the deliberately accepted residual risk, so the work executes as two focused plans.

nodes.label: Threat A — local malware as the same user
nodes.rationale: Stealing the six persist: session cookies is full account takeover; the binary can also be abused as a code-execution vehicle or its files tampered with.
nodes.norm_label: threat a — local malware as the same user

nodes.label: Threat B — hostile web content inside a service view
nodes.rationale: An XSSed or MITMed service escaping the view, abusing the IPC surface, or navigating the view (with its preload attached) to an attacker origin.
nodes.norm_label: threat b — hostile web content inside a service view

nodes.label: Threat C — tampered app/update supply chain
nodes.rationale: Reachable by a local attacker; addressed by SHA-pinning actions and build-provenance attestation.
nodes.norm_label: threat c — tampered app/update supply chain

nodes.label: [Critical] No Electron fuses configured
nodes.rationale: Insecure defaults ship: runAsNode/NODE_OPTIONS/--inspect make the binary a Node interpreter and debug target, cookies are plaintext SQLite in userData, and asar integrity is unvalidated. Single highest-payoff change for threat A.

nodes.label: [High] shell.openExternal with no scheme allowlist
nodes.rationale: views.ts:72 — a hostile page's window.open hands any scheme (file:, smb:, custom) to the OS; fix opens only http:/https:.

nodes.label: [High] Permission handler grants camera/mic with no origin check
nodes.rationale: views.ts:44 — validate the requesting origin against the service's own origin and grant only the permissions a service actually needs.
nodes.norm_label: [high] permission handler grants camera/mic with no origin check

nodes.label: [High] No navigation containment on service views
nodes.rationale: A hostile page can navigate the top-level view (preload rides along) to an attacker origin and persist as a phishing surface; the allowlist must include each service's real auth-redirect hosts, verified by live login, so this is the highest-effort item and is sequenced last.
nodes.norm_label: [high] no navigation containment on service views

nodes.label: [Medium] IPC has no sender/origin validation
nodes.rationale: Page JS cannot currently reach privileged channels (the preload's ipcRenderer is closure-bound, not on window) except the intentional Notification shim, but there is zero defense in depth; fix classifies channels shell-only vs service and matches serviceId to the sending view.

nodes.label: [Medium] No rate limit on notification:fired
nodes.rationale: A hostile page using the Notification shim can spam native banners; fix is a per-service minimum interval in the router.

nodes.label: [Medium] Release supply chain (mutable action tags, no provenance)
nodes.rationale: SHA-pin every action in .github/workflows/release.yml and add build-provenance attestation.
nodes.norm_label: [medium] release supply chain (mutable action tags, no provenance)

nodes.label: [Low] Renderer CSP tightening
nodes.rationale: object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-src 'none' — defense in depth only; the renderer is not attacker-controlled.

nodes.label: Accepted residual risk (same-user malware, notarization out of scope)
nodes.rationale: Malware on an unlocked machine can keylog, screen-capture, and relaunch with --remote-debugging-port regardless of any fix; the fuses close only the silent, no-relaunch paths. Developer ID notarization ($99/yr) is a distribution-trust measure, not a local-tamper fix, and the asar-integrity fuse covers tampering more cheaply. deleteAppDataOnUninstall:false is likewise intentional for session retention.
nodes.norm_label: accepted residual risk (same-user malware, notarization out of scope)

nodes.label: [High] 'Close to tray' off bricks the app
nodes.rationale: tray.ts:58 / index.ts:110 — the window is destroyed but the process keeps running, so broadcast() and tray handlers throw; fix quits outright and guards with isDestroyed().
nodes.norm_label: [high] 'close to tray' off bricks the app

nodes.label: [High] Crash-reload safety cap defeated
nodes.rationale: resilience.ts:27 — any successful did-finish-load resets the attempt counter, so a page that loads then repeatedly dies reloads forever; fix resets only after a minimum uptime dwell.

nodes.label: [High/Medium] Messenger count() style/layout sweep every 2s
nodes.rationale: messenger.ts:12 calls getComputedStyle twice per read row over overlapping element sets; fix is a single traversal computing style once per element, behaviour-preserving (the fixture still yields 3). Deeper selector narrowing needs live DOM.

nodes.label: [Medium] startReadyPoll never stops on logged-out pages
nodes.rationale: ready.ts:31 — the 250 ms poll runs forever if ready() never turns true; bound it to roughly the wake timeout since a late reveal cannot re-cover the current load anyway.
nodes.norm_label: [medium] startreadypoll never stops on logged-out pages

nodes.label: [Medium] Stale reporting has no dedup → broadcast storm
nodes.rationale: runner.ts:47 / state.ts:29 — a persistently failing recipe fires a full ShellState broadcast and React re-render every tick; report stale only on the transition and skip setRuntime notification on a no-op patch.
nodes.norm_label: [medium] stale reporting has no dedup → broadcast storm

nodes.label: [Medium] Window resize re-bounds every view per event
nodes.rationale: views.ts:31 — coalesce layout() to one trailing call per burst.
nodes.norm_label: [medium] window resize re-bounds every view per event

nodes.label: [Medium] Corrupt settings.json bricks startup
nodes.rationale: settings.ts:9 normalize assumes order is an array, so a bad file throws on every hot path; coerce each field with a per-field default fallback.

nodes.label: [Low] connectShell drops the IPC unsubscribe
nodes.rationale: store.ts:14 / App.tsx:13 — under StrictMode two shell:state listeners register; return the unsubscribe and use it as the effect cleanup.

nodes.label: [Low] trustedClick deferred setVisible use-after-destroy
nodes.rationale: views.ts:116 — track the timer, clear it in destroy(), and guard with isDestroyed().

nodes.label: [Low] Runner busy flag can wedge on a hung count()
nodes.rationale: runner.ts:19 — race count() against a timeout so a hung tick clears busy and reports stale.
nodes.norm_label: [low] runner busy flag can wedge on a hung count()

nodes.label: [Low] Badge-label logic duplicated with divergent caps
nodes.rationale: badges.ts:19 caps 9+ while ServiceTile.tsx caps 99+; one shared formatter and one threshold (plus removing the dead isQuitting() export).
nodes.norm_label: [low] badge-label logic duplicated with divergent caps

nodes.label: [Low, Accept] neverHibernate defaults true for all services
nodes.rationale: types.ts:57 — hibernation is effectively disabled and every enabled service stays resident; kept as a product decision because a live count/notify per enabled service is the intended behaviour. Not a correctness bug.
nodes.norm_label: [low, accept] neverhibernate defaults true for all services

nodes.label: Hardening testing strategy
nodes.rationale: Pure logic moves into lib/-style helpers with vitest tests; thin wiring is covered by e2e smoke plus manual checks; config changes (fuses, workflow pinning) are verified out-of-band because they cannot be unit-tested, and navigation containment needs a live login per service.

nodes.norm_label: notification icons shipped unpacked via extraresources
